statement.detailedDescription:
I am writing to dispute a transaction that appeared on my recent statement. On January 30, 2026, a charge of $320.00 was made to 'Retail Store'. I absolutely did not make this purchase, nor was I in possession of my Mastercard at the time of the transaction.

My wallet, containing my Mastercard, was unfortunately lost on or around January 28, 2026. I realized it was missing and reported the card lost and stolen to the bank on February 1, 2026, as soon as I became aware of its absence and after reviewing my online banking statement where I saw this unauthorized transaction. I was shocked to see this particular transaction as it was processed with a chip and PIN, which I believed should have prevented unauthorized use. I never shared my PIN with anyone, and I was not present at the 'Retail Store' on January 30, 2026. I have no knowledge of how my PIN could have been compromised.

I confirm that I did not authorize this transaction, and it was performed without my knowledge or consent while my card was lost. I request a full investigation into this fraudulent activity and a credit for the disputed amount.
statement.merchantResponseSummary: N/A - Cardholder did not contact merchant due to nature of fraud.
statement.requestedResolution: Full credit for the unauthorized charge of $320.00.
statement.cardholderDeclaration: I declare that the information provided in this statement is true, complete, and accurate to the best of my knowledge and belief.

bankInternalNotes.riskAssessment: High. Cardholder reported card lost/stolen after the transaction but prior to knowing about this specific transaction, consistent with fraud. The claim of a compromised PIN for a chip/PIN transaction is concerning but not uncommon in lost/stolen scenarios.
bankInternalNotes.recommendedAction: Initiate chargeback under Mastercard Reason Code 4871. Cardholder's timeline and details align with a genuine lost/stolen scenario where the PIN was compromised.
